topic: Naruto's childhood pranks were a symptom of the isolation caused by Minato's sealing plan, not comic relief, and that same kid becomes the village's hero
title: Naruto's Childhood Pranks Were Never About Being Funny
description: Minato's final wish was for the village to treat his son like a hero. Most of Konoha ignored it instead, and that isolation explains every prank Naruto pulled as a kid. From the full story: Minato Sealed The Nine-Tails Inside Naruto On Purpose.
comment: Did Konoha fail Naruto, or was his isolation just the price of Minato's plan? Pick one.

lines.text: Naruto's pranks as a kid were never about being funny.

shot.fallback: mischievous child grinning after a prank

lines.text: Minato's final wish was for the village to treat his son like a hero, not a container.

shot.fallback: elderly leader addressing a worried village

lines.text: Most of Konoha ignores that request completely, for years.

shot.fallback: crowd of villagers whispering and glaring

lines.text: They don't know the full story, only that a monster tore through their home the night he was born.
Some villagers openly treat him like the Nine-Tails itself, not the boy carrying half of it.

shot.fallback: small child being avoided by adults on a street

lines.text: That isolation is the real reason behind every single prank he pulls as a kid.

shot.fallback: lonely child sitting apart from playing classmates

lines.text: He's not causing chaos for fun. He's trying to get noticed by people who look away from him instead.

shot.fallback: young boy watching others laugh together, excluded

lines.text: Years later, that same lonely kid becomes the one person the whole village depends on.

shot.fallback: confident young hero standing tall over a battlefield

lines.text: Because Naruto's pranks as a kid were never about being funny...

shot.fallback: child grinning mischievously in an empty street
